10.1002_adma.75335: Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.
10.1021_acs.est.6c10822: Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3-SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni-Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2-, O22-, and surface -OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.
10.1021_acsnano.5c00143: A proton battery is considered as a promising energy storage solution with the merits of fast kinetics, high safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. The realization of these merits depends on the exploration of the appropriate and high-performance electrode materials. Although many anode materials of proton batteries have been reported, a dedicated summary of the progress, challenges, and prospects of anode materials for proton batteries has not been reported. Through discussions on the proton storage mechanisms, advantages and limitations of various anode materials, optimization strategies to boost their proton storage capability, and their potential applications, this review seeks to provide a comprehensive theoretical foundation and practical guidance for future research and development of proton battery technology. First, the preparation methods and proton storage mechanism of anode materials have been discussed. Then, the limitations and optimization strategies have been summarized. After that, the next section elaborately focuses on the proton storage performance of different types of anode materials. Finally, the challenges and prospects of anode materials for proton batteries have been proposed. This review aims to provide insight into the efficient design and optimization of anode materials for practical applications of proton batteries.
10.1039_d5ta03021h: Key features of double-atom catalysts are revealed through DFT-integrated machine learning analysis, and a new ML-based screening framework is developed to enable rapid identification of efficient catalysts for CO 2 RR, HER, and OER.
